display.title: Episode 383: The King and the Shabbos Candles
display.summary_short: Torah, davening and kindness, the three legs the world stands on; the story of a king who banned candles until a Shabbos candle saved his life; and why girls light their own Shabbos candles.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 24 Sivan 5749, as summer vacation begins. Uncle Yossi explains the Mishnah in Pirkei Avos that the world stands on three things: Torah, avodah and gemilus chasadim. Like a stool, or a potato standing on three toothpicks, it needs all three every day, so in camp or in the country children should take along a Chumash, a siddur and a tzedakah pushka, and give tzedakah before davening and before Shabbos. After the Hakochainik march, two sisters lead the Shema. In the story, a king whose new study burns down bans all candles in his city. The Jews pray and resolve to beautify the mitzvah of Shabbos candles, with every daughter lighting too. Lost in a snowstorm on a Friday evening, the king follows the light of Shabbos candles in a cabin outside the city, is welcomed to a Shabbos table, and cancels his decree. Uncle Yossi then teaches that children bring their parents nachas through kibbud av va'em, and that a girl lighting her own Shabbos candle beside her mother brings light into the world. Children are invited to write about lighting for the first time.
display.lesson: Every day needs Torah, davening and kindness; and the light of Shabbos candles, lit by every Jewish girl, brings blessing and protection.

The king is thrown from his horse and lost in a snowstorm.
